amendment: Added before any model was run on a TEST episode: two port episodes added (santos_2025, nhavasheva_2021, both TRAIN by the unchanged split rule) for regional spread; unsourced candidates recorded in 'excluded'. Rule changes are in rule_val01-v1.json (control pool, placebo windows, strata, per-place table). The TRAIN aggregate of the first collection had been seen when this amendment was written; the changes follow the design aim (generalise across ports, kinds and regions), not a number.
label: BACKTEST - historical disruptions with public PortWatch coverage; never merged with the live Ledger.
note: INPUTS ONLY. Nothing in this file is an outcome: no PortWatch value was read to write it. capacity_loss is taken from a stated source, derived by arithmetic from a stated source, or (one case) flagged MODELED. Source verification: 'fetched' = the page was retrieved and the cited fact read; 'search_result' = the fact is quoted in a web-search result for that URL but the page itself could not be fetched (403/503) or was not fetched; 'prior_curated_record' = taken from an earlier curated record of the same event in this repo (path given), retrieved on the date shown.

split.rule: sha256('val01-split-v1:' + episode_id) first 8 hex digits as an integer, modulo 100; < 60 -> TRAIN, else TEST
split.note: The seed string was fixed before any outcome was collected and is not tuned; the resulting 7 TRAIN / 5 TEST split is whatever the hash gives.

capacity_loss_basis_classes.STATED_CLOSURE: sources state the place/terminal was closed or operations halted; capacity_loss = 1.0 (kind closure; the engine forces 1.0)
capacity_loss_basis_classes.MODELED: no sourced figure exists; a modelling assumption, never to be presented as sourced

episodes.title: Shanghai COVID lockdown, April 2022 (container calls)

capacity_loss_basis.derivation: Drewry via Seatrade/WorldPorts: expected daily container handling capacity about 100,000 TEU in April 2022, a decline of 25 percent from normal; Shanghai volumes fell 25 percent month on month. (Alternative figure not used: Ministry of Transport, April 2022 throughput 82.4 percent of April 2021.)

episodes.duration_basis: April 2022: both quantified sources (25 percent capacity decline; 82.4 percent of last year) describe April. The end date of the lockdown itself (1 June) was NOT verified, so the stated scope of the figure is used.

sources.supports: 25 percent capacity decline (page fetch returned HTTP 403)
same Drewry figure, republished (page fetch returned HTTP 403)

episodes.title: Ningbo-Zhoushan Meishan terminal closure, August 2021 (container calls)

capacity_loss_basis.derivation: Meishan terminal closed (STATED_CLOSURE) and accounts for about a quarter of the Ningbo-Zhoushan port's container throughput (Caixin/Bloomberg); Argus puts it near 20 percent (not used). capacity_loss = 0.25 for the port.

episodes.duration_basis: closed 11 Aug; partial vessel operations from 18 Aug; official said still closed 23 Aug; Argus: closed two weeks to 25 Aug. 14 d is the Argus stated duration.

sources.supports: closure 11 Aug 2021; partial resumption 18 Aug; about a quarter of throughput
closed two weeks until 25 Aug; about 20 percent of volumes

episodes.title: Beirut port explosion

capacity_loss_basis.derivation: Lebanese army commander: port operating capacity about 45 percent as of 27 Aug 2020 (Arab News via Maritime Executive); 1 - 0.45 = 0.55. The container terminal alone was reported at about 80 percent (not used: the metric counts all vessels).

episodes.duration_basis: 4 Aug to 27 Aug 2020, the date the 45 percent figure was stated; the port had not recovered by then, so the duration is a LOWER BOUND.

sources.supports: 45 percent operating capacity at 27 Aug; container terminal back 10 Aug at about 80 percent
container lines resume calls as terminal restarts
port back to business, 1 Sep 2020

episodes.title: Key Bridge collapse, Port of Baltimore

capacity_loss_basis.derivation: Maryland Port Administration, 26 Mar 2024: vessel traffic suspended indefinitely. Temporary limited channels reopened in stages from about 1 Apr; the full 700 ft x 50 ft channel reopened 10 Jun 2024. Treating the whole span as a full closure overstates the loss after the first temporary channels; this is a stated simplification, not an observation.

episodes.duration_basis: 26 Mar to 10 Jun 2024 (full channel reopening, USACE)
episodes.note_tier: sea_baltimore is a SHELL-tier node: engine runs are allowed; Ledger locks are not.

sources.supports: vessel traffic suspended indefinitely 26 Mar 2024
full restoration of the Fort McHenry channel, 10 Jun 2024
inbound and outbound vessel traffic suspended until further notice

episodes.title: Cyclone Tauktae, Nhava Sheva (JNPT), May 2021

capacity_loss_basis.derivation: S&P Global: JNPT suspended berthing from late Saturday night 15 May 2021, planned to sail out all vessels at berth by 23:00 on 15 May, suspended operations and evacuated the dockyard on Sunday evening; berthing at all terminals could resume from 01:00 on Tuesday 18 May depending on weather (a plan; the actual restart time was not confirmed). Maersk later reported JNPT back to normal operations.

episodes.duration_basis: 23:00 IST 15 May to the planned restart 01:00 IST 18 May; the actual restart is NOT confirmed, so this is the planned duration
